title: Web Application Security
summary: Understand common web risks, testing methodology, secure design, and remediation.

lessons.title: Input handling and parameterized queries
lessons.summary: Trace untrusted input and prevent injection flaws.
lessons.content: Treat all client-controlled input as untrusted. Prefer parameterized queries, strict validation, safe output encoding, and least-privilege database accounts. Build regression tests around the underlying trust boundary.

quiz.question: Which approach is the primary defense against SQL injection?
quiz.explanation: Parameterized queries separate query structure from untrusted values.

lessons.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) and Content Security Policy
lessons.summary: Contextual output encoding and strict CSP mitigation strategies.
lessons.content: XSS occurs when an application includes untrusted data in an HTTP response without proper validation or escaping. Contextual encoding (HTML, attribute, JS, CSS) alongside a strict nonced Content-Security-Policy (CSP) drastically reduces exploitation surface.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a Content-Security-Policy header?
options: To restrict the sources from which scripts, styles, and other assets can be loaded or executed
quiz.explanation: CSP is an HTTP response header that restricts resource origins and prevents execution of inline untrusted scripts.
